text:
Detroit controlled this game and still lost it in the span of 92 seconds. Cole Perfetti deflected one in on the power play at 13:04 of the first, and Kyle Connor backhanded home another with the man advantage at 14:36. Winnipeg scored three times on four power plays, including Connor's snap shot early in the second that made it 3-0, and that was nearly the whole difference.

Everything else belonged to the Red Wings. They outshot Winnipeg 36 to 27 and outattempted them 78 to 53, and their expected goals of 4.91 against 2.83 came out ahead in every period. At even strength it was 2.91 to 1.44. Running the chances through a thousand simulated replays, Detroit wins 82 percent of them. Stuart Skinner is the reason this one wasn't a rout: he faced shots worth 4.91 expected goals, allowed two, and finished 2.91 goals better than expected. John Gibson, by contrast, was slightly below par, letting in three on 2.63 expected.

The comeback arrived late. Viktor Arvidsson cut it to 3-1 on a deflection with the power play at 16:52 of the second, and Emmitt Finnie's wrist shot at 4:56 of the third made it 3-2. Michael Brandsegg-Nygård (six shots, 1.17 individual expected goals) set up the second one, and Detroit had the better of play for the remaining 15 minutes without finding a tying goal. Connor finished with two goals and an assist, and Perfetti added a goal and two helpers. Winnipeg took the points on a night when Detroit mostly out-played it.
